captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a double-ended measuring spoon or cup pair. It features two hemispherical measuring cups of different volumes on either end of a long, rigid connecting handle. The handle has a triangular cross-section (tribar) for structural rigidity and ease of cleaning, while each cup is supported by a cylindrical pillar base that ensures they can sit flat on a surface.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric double-ended measuring cup system in OpenSCAD. The design should allow the user to input two target volumes (v0 and v1) in cubic millimeters, automatically calculate the corresponding spherical cup radii, and connect them with a customizable handle length and wall thickness, with an option for a rigid triangular connector bar.
captions.factory: The script calculates cup radii using a mathematical function based on the input volumes. The main assembly module 'cuppair' uses 'difference' to hollow out the cups, combining a 'spherepair' and 'supportpillars' (created using 'hull' on cylinders) with a 'tribar' connector. The 'tribar' module is constructed by applying 'hull' on three rotated 3-sided cylinders ($fn=3) to form a rigid triangular prism. Finally, a large cube is subtracted from the top of the entire assembly to slice the spheres in half, creating the open cup shapes.
